schemes.participation_data: More than 2,000 students have completed the programme since 2013 (cumulative participants; 2026 news item).
schemes.named_partners: 2026 news item: Birmingham City FC, Conde Nast, Expedia Group, HSBC, Siemens, Transport for West Midlands, West Midlands Combined Authority; employer partners page lists 8 supporters for June 2026 incl. new partner BBC Studios Drama Productions.
schemes.description: One-week, full-time (09:00-17:00) on-campus programme for first-year undergraduates. Students are matched to a sustainability/social theme and placed in small interdisciplinary teams; the challenge question, set by one of the employer partners, is revealed on day one. Each challenge is supported by an industry professional and a team of academics. Teams produce a solution and give an assessed group video presentation to peers, industry professionals and academics on the final day, plus an individual self-evaluation.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Registered first-year undergraduates on any course (incl. Erasmus students) at the Birmingham (Edgbaston) campus
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: First-year UG, Birmingham campus only; must attend every day of the week; Birmingham Scholars and students from IMD Quintile 1 neighbourhoods encouraged/get early enrolment (16 March 2026; general enrolment 30 March 2026).
schemes.credit_assessment: Non-credit-bearing; recorded as a pass/fail module on the University transcript. Group video presentation 50% + individual self-evaluation 50%.
schemes.project_evidence: Defined challenge question per team, solution developed over the week and delivered as an assessed group video presentation [1][2].
schemes.group_evidence: Students work in small interdisciplinary teams/groups with students from across the university; assessed group presentation [1][3].
schemes.employer_evidence: Employer partners set the challenges ('seven employer-set challenges' in the 2026 news item), an industry professional supports each challenge, and teams present to industry professionals on the final day [1][4][5].
schemes.partner_role: Set the challenge question; industry professional supports each challenge team; industry professionals attend/receive final presentations.
schemes.deliverable: Group video presentation of solution; individual self-evaluation
schemes.latest_evidenced_year: 2026 (8-12 June 2026 run; a 7-11 June 2027 run was also reported)
schemes.unresolved: Partner count differs (7 in news item vs 8 on partner page for 2026). Annual places not published. 2027 dates came from a search summary of the project page and are not separately verified.

profile_md:
**Birmingham** has several distributed live-project routes. Most are **short, extracurricular and centrally run**, with smaller programme-embedded provision in the Business School.

- **Central (Careers Network):**
  - **The Birmingham Project** is open to all first-year undergraduates on the Edgbaston campus. It is optional, non-credit and recorded as pass/fail on the transcript. Interdisciplinary teams spend one full-time week in June on challenges set by 7–8 employer partners in 2026 (e.g. HSBC, Siemens, Transport for West Midlands, West Midlands Combined Authority). Each challenge has an industry professional, and teams finish with a group video presentation to industry and academics. More than 2,000 students have taken part since 2013.
  - The **Masters Consultancy Challenge** is selective and open to taught postgraduates. Interdisciplinary groups work for 3 weeks on a Turner & Townsend challenge and present to an industry and University panel.
  - The **Impact Challenge** is a paid, week-long programme for widening-participation finalists and penultimate-year students. Teams work on employer-set projects, mostly for charities and social enterprises.
- **Business School:**
  - The **Capgemini Community Challenge** is a week at Capgemini Telford in which undergraduate teams consult for charity clients.
  - The **MSc Strategic Marketing and Consulting** includes a group consultancy project for real organisations, but its current-year delivery is unconfirmed.
  - **Masters/MBA Company Projects** tackle live business challenges, but it is unclear whether they are done in groups.
- **Engineering:** MEng group design projects are only described as "industry-linked". The **Chemical Engineering** design project is recorded as Unclear.

**Other areas (reduced depth):** a Law Pro Bono/FLAG clinic (student pairs advising real clients under solicitor supervision) is recorded but its external-organisation status is Unclear; a compulsory Year 2 Mathematics industry-problem module is a lead only. Social science, Biosciences, Geography and Health searches found no client-based group modules.

**Limits:** reduced-depth review; further departmental routes likely.
gaps: Further departmental instances likely. Engineering group design projects lack evidence of industry-set briefs. Current-year evidence missing for SMC MSc and Company Projects. Maths Mathematical Challenge module partner/team format unverified. Education, Psychology and Biosciences only lightly searched. Birmingham Project partner count conflict (7 vs 8). Capgemini eligibility conflict.
